items.title: Dozens of women reveal dark side of growing up in Byron Bay 'paradise'
items.description: Rachel Kila has waived her right to anonymity to join dozens of others speaking out about the experiences of young girls in Byron Bay in the early 2000s, where they say it became normalised for older boys and men to groom and have sex with girls then publicly humiliate them.

items.title: Live: Pauline Hanson says she has 'the ability' to be PM
items.description: Pauline Hanson says she has the ability to lead the nation as prime minister but admits she was shocked by a poll that suggested One Nation had pulled ahead of Labor. Follow live.

items.title: One Nation overtakes Labor for first time as young Australians reject budget
items.description: Labor's federal budget is falling flat with its target demographic as millennials say they would rather vote for One Nation than Labor or the Greens, according to a new Redbridge poll.

items.title: Government loses bid to keep terror funding documents secret
items.description: Commissioner Virginia Bell says the documents will provide a comparison of the resourcing given to counterterrorism agencies before and after August 2024, when the terror threat level was raised to "probable".

items.title: Woman charged with joining Islamic State 'renounces' terror group
items.description: Melbourne woman Rayann El Houli appears in court for a bail hearing after being charged with travelling to Syria to join the Islamic State group, before returning home last year.

items.title: Police unlawfully arrested this man, broke his ribs, then charged him with assault
items.description: After fracturing about a dozen of a man's ribs and puncturing his lung, police officers discussed how to explain what happened to him.

items.title: Nancy Guthrie's whereabouts remain a mystery four months after vanishing
items.description: It has been four months since Nancy Guthrie, the mother of America's Today show co-host Savannah Guthrie, was reported missing. This is what we know about the alleged abduction.

items.title: Why is Labor spending its political majority on this tax reform?
items.description: Why has Labor decided to spend the political capital of a large majority on a minor change to capital gains tax on businesses?

items.title: Almost 70,000 without power after storms tear through southern WA
items.description: Tens of thousands of homes are without power and the SES receives hundreds of calls for help, with the roof torn off one Perth apartment building, after WA's southern half is hammered by more severe weather.

items.title: Sydney and Melbourne property values drop as housing market stalls in May
items.description: Australia's housing market continues to lose momentum, with national home values flatlining in May as higher interest rates, weak confidence and proposed property tax changes weigh on demand.

items.title: Live: ASX lower despite Wall St gains, AUD flat, oil higher
items.description: The Australian share market has begun winter with a slight decline, with the ASX 200 in negative territory to start the new trading week. The weakness comes despite a solid finish on Wall Street on Friday, with the Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all ending higher. Follow our live business blog.

items.title: 'I won't be a yes man': Co-chair of ACT Reconciliation council resigns
items.description: ACT Reconciliation Council co-chair Selina Walker resigns, saying she has lost faith in the territory government's approach to Indigenous affairs.

items.title: Search for man missing in East Arnhem Land ends after nine days
items.description: After a nine-day operation covering more than 1,300 square kilometres of land, the search for a 31-year-old man in East Arnhem Land has been stood down.

items.title: Three-year-old child dies in Melbourne house fire
items.description: A child has died in a house fire in Werribee and another person has been taken to hospital with serious injuries.

items.title: One-third of Ian Thorpe's life was in the spotlight, and it took its toll
items.description: Ian Thorpe became a global star as a teenager, attracting both opportunities and scrutiny. Now, he wishes he'd done some things differently.

items.title: The 'black hole' of binding financial agreements
items.description: Binding financial agreements take time and money to obtain. Here's how they work.

items.title: Roadside stalls are booming, with 45,000 members in one group alone
items.description: Nestled away in the Adelaide Hills are dozens of roadside stalls dedicated to local produce, including baked goods and bouquets, and business is booming.

items.title: 'Bittersweet': These unique trees only flower once in their life — then die
items.description: About 20 Gebang palms have flowered in Darwin in a rare spectacle, reaffirming the local council's plans to foster a new generation of the trees.

items.title: 'Loving' parents not at fault for deaths of children left in hot cars, coroner finds
items.description: The deaths of two children who were left in cars during hot weather were the result of their parents' memory failure, a NSW coroner finds.

items.title: House fire allegedly started by half-brother of murdered teen Angus Beaumont
items.description: A fire that destroyed a Redcliffe home and damaged two other was allegedly started by the half-brother of murdered teenager Angus Beaumont.

items.title: Public servant to take SA government to court over golf course redevelopment
items.description: An Adelaide man alleges the state government failed to properly refer the controversial North Adelaide Golf Course to the federal environment minister for approval.

items.title: Olympic stadium work underway as premier warns off protesters
items.description: The last protesters were removed from Victoria Park in the early hours of Monday morning.

items.title: Broome local cringes as AI sells WA's north 'as something it's not'
items.description: A wave of AI-generated videos posted to social media causes a stir among tour operators in WA's north. They say the content does not accurately portray the region and threatens the preservation of Indigenous culture.

items.title: Thousands of green sea turtle hatchlings swim to sea in a conservation win
items.description: The project at Raine Island, where 90 per cent of northern green sea turtles nest, has been working for a decade to improve hatching success.

items.title: Shein, Kmart fight back against Qld retailer in intellectual property dispute
items.description: Shein and Kmart have fired back at Sabo Skirt in an intellectual property dispute, saying the designs have been accused of copying are substantially similar to pre-existing designs.
